status_summary: The administration's main China trade tools have been the broad measures the essay argues against: Executive Order 14257 (signed 2025-04-02) set a baseline duty on all trading partners with country-specific rates, and later Section 232 and Section 301 actions apply to whole sectors or economies (see c26-02 and c26-04). Firm-level action has continued through export controls framed around national security rather than unfair trade practices: a BIS rule effective 2025-03-25 (90 FR 14046) added 11 Chinese entities and one in Taiwan to the Entity List for supporting military modernization through AI, chips and supercomputers, without citing intellectual property theft. A BIS interim final rule effective 2025-09-29 (90 FR 47201) extended Entity List restrictions to affiliates at least 50 percent owned by listed parties, and BIS suspended it on 2025-11-12 until 2026-11-09.

timeline.event: S. 330, the Combatting China's Pilfering of Intellectual Property Act, was introduced in the Senate and referred to the Foreign Relations Committee; it would require sanctions, including asset blocking and visa bars, on Chinese persons found to have engaged in a pattern of significant theft of U.S. intellectual property.
BIS added 12 entities (11 in China, 1 in Taiwan) to the Entity List, effective this date.
Executive Order 14257 (signed 2025-04-02) imposing a baseline and country-specific reciprocal tariff was published.
BIS published the Affiliates rule extending Entity List restrictions to 50 percent-owned affiliates.
BIS published a final rule suspending the affiliates rule for one year, until 2026-11-09 unless extended.

title: Target individual Chinese firms for unfair practices instead of blanket sector tariffs
uncertainties: This is a judgment call: firm-level Entity List actions against Chinese companies continue, so a reader could stage the record in_progress with a partial match; it is staged diverged because the essay's central ask is to use firm targeting instead of blanket tariffs, and those listings cite national security rather than unfair trade practices. Only a few Entity List rules were read; others in 2025 and 2026 (including removals such as Arrow Electronics entries on 2026-08-21) were not reviewed. OFAC designations of Chinese firms were not searched. The affiliates rule suspension ends on 2026-11-09 unless extended. The first-term practice the essay cites was not checked. Checked systematically on 2026-10-18: Federal Register search of BIS Entity List documents, the BIS proposed-rule listing (zero; agenda listing not browsable), a congress.gov and GovInfo search, USTR, Treasury and BIS newsrooms, and one news search found no executive action targeting firms on grounds of intellectual property theft or unfair trade practices; Entity List actions found are national security listings, and USTR's December 2025 semiconductor action again targets a sector. One introduced bill points toward the recommendation: S. 330 (introduced 2025-01-30, referred to the Senate Foreign Relations Committee) would require the President to block the property of, and deny visas to, Chinese persons found to have engaged in or benefited from a pattern of significant theft of U.S. intellectual property; its bill status also lists a 2025-07-23 Senate Small Business Committee hearing. Diverged is kept because the operative policy remains the blanket measures the essay opposes; proposed 5 is the other defensible call if the bill is weighed as a step toward firm-level targeting.
